To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

anti-inflammatory and disease-modifying drugs inhibit the production of the chemotactic cytokine MCP-1 and the chemotactic and angiogenic cytokine IL-8, and that dexametasone is the most effective inhibitor of MCP-1 production.
the production of the chemotactic cytokine MCP-1 by rheumatoid arthritis synoviocytes can be inhibited by glucocorticoids and by the gold compound GST, while MTX is inactive.
anti-rheumatic agents differentially inhibit the production of chemokines by RA synoviocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of anti- rheumatic drugs on the production of MCP1 and IL-1 by cultured RA synovial cells.
the production of chemotactic proteins by synoviocytes and the effect of anti-rheumatoid drugs on this production.
the role of monocyte chemo-attractant protein 2 (MCP-2) in inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

anti-rheumatic drug effects on the production of chemotactic proteins by activated RA synoviocytes are not uniform and that the anti-rheumatoid action of dexamethasome is due to its capacity to inhibit the production of IL8 and MCP- 1.
the production of both MCP-1 and interleukine-8 by synoviocytes is inhibited by dexamethasome and gold sodium thiolmalate, but not by methotrexate.
dexamethazone is the most effective drug in inhibiting chemokine synthesis by RA synoviocytes, and this may contribute to its anti-rheumatic activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

anti-rheumatic agents, including glucocorticoids, are capable of reducing the production of chemotactic proteins by synoviocytes and may therefore reduce the recruitment of inflammatory mononuclear and polymorphonuclear cells into the arthic joint.
the anti-rheumatoid drugs dexamethasome (DEX) and gold sodium thiolmate (GST) inhibit the synthesis of monocyte chemo-attractant protein 2 (MCP-2) and interleukine 8 (IL8) by synoviocytes.

dexamethosone and GST are the most efficient drugs to inhibit the production of chemotactic proteins by RA synoviocytes, while MTX and non-steroidal anti-rheumatic agents have no or only weak effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production of chemotactic proteins by activated synoviocytes is inhibited by anti-rheumatoid agents.
the production of chemotactic proteins by RA synoviocytes is not only a marker of the activated state of these cells but also contributes to the perpetuation of inflammatory reactions in the joint.
the production of chemotactic mediators is a common feature of RA synovial cells and that anti-rheumatic compounds may act in part through the inhibition of chemotactic protein production.
